title: Al-Fajr 89:7-12 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 2: Al-Fajr and the families of madd
source: Written for quran/y4 lesson 27 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Fajr 89:7-12 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 27. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: إِرَمَ ذَاتِ ٱلْعِمَادِ (٧) ٱلَّتِى لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِى ٱلْبِلَٰدِ (٨) وَثَمُودَ ٱلَّذِينَ جَابُوا۟ ٱلصَّخْرَ بِٱلْوَادِ (٩) وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِى ٱلْأَوْتَادِ (١٠) ٱلَّذِينَ طَغَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْبِلَٰدِ (١١) فَأَكْثَرُوا۟ فِيهَا ٱلْفَسَادَ (١٢)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: The likes of whom had never been created in the land?
And [with] Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley?
And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes? -
[All of] whom oppressed within the lands

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Moon letter: hamza; natural madd at the end

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Fajr 89:7-12 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 89:7-12 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 89:7-12 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Write the three peoples named in 89:6 to 10.
questions.a: 'Aad, Thamud and Pharaoh (Fir'awn) with his people.

questions.q: Find two heavy letters and one qalqalah in 89:7 to 12.
questions.a: For example: heavy ص and خ in ٱلصَّخْرَ, ط in طَغَوْا۟; qalqalah on ق in يُخْلَقْ.

questions.q: Which people 'carved out the rocks in the valley' (89:9)?
questions.a: A) Thamud. 89:9: 'And Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley.'

questions.q: Think again: 'Aad, Thamud and Pharaoh had pillars, carved rocks and great power. Why did their power not save them?
questions.a: They oppressed people and spread corruption (89:11 to 12). No power protects anyone from Allah.
